items.notes: Two hand-reflowed boards. On both, the DS2482 1-Wire bridge answers at `0x18` and the ADS1115 at `0x48`, their factory-default addresses, when the board is connected to the hub's Qwiic port.

Default registers read correctly, a written register reads back, and all four inputs convert. Nothing is connected to the inputs yet (the sensor connectors are not fitted), so the readings are floating values of about 0.6 V. The solder joints of the input pins have not been checked by driving them.
Reset, configuration write and read-back, and the 1-Wire reset pulse all work with no short on the 1-Wire line. No 1-Wire sensor has been attached yet.

items.feature: Differential I2C link over RJ45 (3 ft cable)
items.notes: One board works from the hub's `J202` over a 3 ft straight cable with nothing on its Qwiic port: the DS2482 and ADS1115 appear on the hub's user bus. A first attempt failed because the PCA9615's five differential-side pins were poorly soldered; reflowing them fixed it. The other board's link is blocked by a solder bridge under the RJ45 jack between pins 3 and 6, found after assembly and being reworked.

items.feature: Differential I2C link over a longer cable
items.notes: Only a 3 ft cable has been tried. A longer cable in a real-world setting is still to do.
The through-hole sensor connectors and the RJ45 jacks are fitted after the surface-mount parts are validated, so no analog or 1-Wire sensor has been connected yet.
